prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the interior of an open refrigerator directly in front of the camera wearer (whose own body and face are behind the viewpoint, with no other people present), where the left fridge wall and upper shelf edge are nearest at roughly 0.2 to 0.3 metres and the recessed shelf compartments sit further back at 0.4 to 0.7 metres. Across frames 1 to 2, a blue-lidded container held by the camera wearer's hand moves away from about 0.2 metres to rest on the lower shelf at roughly 0.45 metres, positioned 0.1 to 0.2 metres in front of a white tub and egg carton on the left and beside a milk jug and bread loaf on the right, all within arm's reach. In frames 3 and 4, the camera wearer's bright right forearm and hand extend forward from the bottom-right at 0.2 to 0.4 metres toward a clear container on the upper shelf above, partially occluding the milk jug and red container behind the arm before the camera turns up and right in frame 5. The map clarifies the continuous 3D depth separation between the protruding upper shelf lip, the foreground arm, and the recessed objects beneath the shelf that have low contrast or shadows in RGB. However, it is unreliable in frame 5 where motion blur flattens the shelf geometry and in the dark rear corners of the lower shelf where depth values drop off sharply into black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects almost nothing of the refrigerator scene in frames 1, 2, and 5, capturing only the large `refrigerator` region (roughly 0.2 to 0.7 metres away) and the camera wearer's `person` right arm extending from the bottom-right foreground (0.2 to 0.4 metres away) in frames 3 and 4. Within frames 3 and 4, the `person` mask reaches upward and left toward the upper shelf within arm's reach, overlapping and occluding the right side of the `refrigerator` mask while no other people or faces are in view. When active in frames 3 and 4, the sharp boundary of the `person` mask isolates the exact 2D silhouette of the camera wearer's reaching arm and hand against the cluttered shelf background more cleanly than the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is highly unreliable across the strip: it misses all shelves and containers in frames 1, 2, and 5, and it severely misclassifies the small round tub on the left as a `bottle` (frames 1, 2, and 4), the egg carton behind the blue lid as a `banana` (frame 1), and the lower-left fridge door hinge area as a `toilet` (frame 4).
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no yellow body skeletons because no other people are present and the camera wearer's torso and head remain behind the egocentric viewpoint, showing only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in frames 3 and 4. In those two frames, the hand is positioned in the upper-center of the view at roughly 0.35 to 0.45 metres from the camera wearer, above the lower-shelf containers and directly in front of the clear container on the upper shelf within arm's reach, with the palm facing left and the thumb extended left while the fingers curl around the container's top edge. Between frames 3 and 4, the hand shifts slightly downward and to the right as it grasps the upper-shelf container, with the wrist connecting toward the unrendered forearm extending out of the bottom-right frame edge. This skeletal representation makes the exact 3D finger articulation and pinch-grip geometry around the translucent container lid easier to see than in the overexposed and motion-blurred RGB frames. The map is unreliable in frames 1 and 2, where it completely misses the camera wearer's hand visible at the bottom edge holding the blue-lidded container, and in frame 5 where the hand has retreated out of view.
